title: Cryptool vs CoinList
content_html:
Cryptool vs CoinList comes down to what you need after the token sale closes. CoinList runs compliant public token sales and gives retail investors access to early-stage projects. Cryptool.io (Cryptool) is a crypto investment operating system that tracks portfolios non-custodially across all chains and wallets, then adds fund administration, syndicate management, vesting schedules and investor reporting in the same place. If you run a fund, a syndicate or a VC portfolio and need to manage allocations and positions after the deal closes, that is where the two products differ.

CoinList is the right answer when you want to participate in token sales as an individual investor or when you are launching a compliant public token sale. Cryptool is the right answer when you need to track a multi-wallet portfolio, manage a fund or syndicate, run your own private raise, or handle vesting and distributions for a group of investors.

What CoinList is good at

CoinList specializes in compliant token sales and early-stage project access. The platform runs token sales that meet regulatory requirements in multiple jurisdictions, handles identity verification for participants, and manages the legal and compliance work that comes with a public sale. Projects use CoinList to reach a large investor base while staying compliant. Retail investors use it to access token sales they would not otherwise see.

CoinList also offers staking for some assets and wallet services. The focus is on the fundraising event itself and getting tokens into the hands of participants. If you are launching a token and need a platform that handles the regulatory side and brings an audience, CoinList does that well.

What Cryptool does differently

Cryptool is built for what happens after the allocation lands. It starts with non-custodial portfolio tracking across all chains and all wallets. Add wallets from MetaMask, Ledger, Trust Wallet or any other provider, and Cryptool reads balances and positions without holding your keys. Your funds stay in your control.

Then it adds the operations layer. Fund administration tools let you track allocations, calculate positions per member, and report to LPs from the same system that holds your portfolio view. Syndicate management handles group investing with per-member allocations and automated distributions. The Raise module runs private fundraising rounds with configurable caps, vesting schedules and identity verification. The OTC marketplace lets you negotiate and settle allocation trades without custody transfer. The Calendar tracks vesting events and raise milestones. Document management stores deal paperwork in one place.

The difference is that Cryptool combines portfolio tracking with the fund-operations work that otherwise means separate systems for each piece. CoinList focuses on the token sale event. Cryptool focuses on the portfolio and allocation management that comes before and after.

Which one should you pick

Pick CoinList if you are launching a token and need a compliant public sale with a built-in investor base. CoinList handles the regulatory work, brings the audience, and manages the distribution. This is their specialty and they do it well.

Pick CoinList if you are a retail investor who wants access to token sales and early-stage projects. The platform gives you entry to deals you would not otherwise see, with the compliance work already done.

Pick Cryptool if you manage a fund, a syndicate or a VC portfolio and need to track holdings across multiple wallets and chains while managing allocations, vesting and investor reporting in the same system. The non-custodial portfolio tracking reads all your wallets without custody transfer, and the fund-operations tools sit in the same place.

Pick Cryptool if you are running a private raise for your own fund or project and need to manage commitments, allocations and distributions without handing over control to a third-party platform. The Raise module runs the whole process, and you keep custody of the funds.

Pick Cryptool if you need an OTC marketplace for allocations alongside your portfolio and fund operations. The Market module handles allocation trading, and settlement happens without custody transfer.

Use both if you participate in CoinList token sales and then need to track those allocations alongside the rest of your portfolio. Connect the wallet that holds your CoinList tokens to Cryptool, and it appears in your consolidated view with everything else.

How they work together

Many funds and syndicates participate in CoinList token sales and then track those allocations in Cryptool. The wallet that receives tokens from a CoinList sale connects to Cryptool like any other wallet, and the positions show up in your portfolio view automatically. Vesting schedules from CoinList sales can be added to the Cryptool Calendar so you see all your unlock dates in one place.

CoinList focuses on the sale event and getting tokens distributed. Cryptool focuses on tracking those tokens alongside everything else you hold, managing allocations across your group, and reporting positions to your LPs. The two products cover different parts of the investment process.

Pricing

CoinList charges fees per token sale, structured as a percentage of funds raised. The exact terms vary by project and sale type.

Cryptool offers plans from $0 for individual users tracking a single wallet, up to Enterprise plans for funds and syndicates managing groups with unlimited members. Fund administration, syndicate management and the Raise module are available on paid plans. Details at cryptool.io/documents/services-pricing.

FAQ

What is the main difference between Cryptool and CoinList?

CoinList runs compliant public token sales and gives investors access to early-stage projects. Cryptool.io is a crypto investment operating system that tracks portfolios non-custodially across all chains and wallets, then adds fund administration, syndicate management, private fundraising, vesting schedules and investor reporting in one platform. CoinList focuses on the token sale event. Cryptool focuses on portfolio and allocation management before and after the sale.

Can I use both CoinList and Cryptool together?

Yes. Many funds and syndicates participate in CoinList token sales and then connect the wallet that receives those tokens to Cryptool for ongoing portfolio tracking and allocation management. The two products cover different parts of the investment process and work well together.

Is Cryptool custodial like CoinList?

No. Cryptool is non-custodial by design. All wallet connections are read-only. Your private keys stay in your control, and Cryptool never holds your funds. CoinList holds funds during token sales and distributions, which is necessary for running compliant public sales.

Does Cryptool run public token sales like CoinList?

No. Cryptool runs private fundraising rounds for funds, syndicates and projects using the Raise module. These are private raises with configurable caps, vesting schedules and identity verification, not public token sales. If you need a compliant public sale with a large investor base, CoinList is the right platform for that.

Can I track CoinList allocations in Cryptool?

Yes. Connect the wallet that holds your CoinList tokens to Cryptool, and the positions appear in your portfolio view automatically. Vesting schedules from CoinList sales can be added to the Cryptool Calendar so all your unlock dates are in one place.

Which platform is better for fund managers?

Cryptool is built for fund managers who need to track portfolios across multiple wallets and chains while managing allocations, vesting and investor reporting in one system. CoinList is built for launching token sales and giving retail investors access to early-stage projects. If you manage a fund or syndicate and need fund administration tools alongside portfolio tracking, Cryptool covers that. If you are launching a public token sale, CoinList covers that.
